newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up at year-high against US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up at year-high against US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at a year-high for the fifth straight day on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market, ending at 8.3026 on Friday from Thursday's 8.3036 against the U.S. dollar.
They said that China's improving international trade balance and less intervention from the central bank had boosted positive expectations of the yuan's trend.
The yuan opened slightly up at an intra-day low of 8.3035 and consolidated around 8.3030 for most of the session, hitting a high of 8.3020.
Trading was more active than yesterday, with most done at 8.3030, traders said.
"The yuan's continuous rises strengthened the confidence of buyers," said one dealer.

"The People's Bank of China intervened less to depress the yuan, which has helped its uptrend over the past week," a second dealer said. "A rebound in the inflation rate limited the central bank's selling of the local unit."
China's retail inflation rate in August increased 1.5 percentage points from July to 8.1 percent, the first upturn since February.
Dealers said they expect the yuan to continue to rise early next week.
The yuan ended slightly up at 7.5755 from 7.5805 against 100 Japanese yen, and down at an intra-day low of 1.0750 from 1.0745 against the Hong Kong dollar.
